newsitem.title: INDIA: India CRISIL launches new equity index.
newsitem.headline: India CRISIL launches new equity index.

text.p: India's top rating agency on Tuesday launched a new equity index that will track shares of multinational companies, the agency said.

The Credit Rating Information Services of India Ltd (CRISIL) said the index -- called CRISIL MNC Index -- comprises 50 listed firms in which foreign holdings were either over 50 percent, or were run by foreign firms.
The index accounts for 92 percent of the market capitalisation of multinational stocks, and represents 85 percent of share transactions in the segment, CRISIL said.
It also launched an index for firms held by Indian business families.
The CRISIL Indian Business Groups Index covers 250 listed firms representing 107 local groups, it said in a statement.
The index represented 99 percent of the share deals in the segment, it said.
The indexes were launched to help fund managers in their asset allocation and segmental exposure decisions, it said.
CRISIL had earlier launched a 500-stock index, a mid-cap 200-stock index and an index that tracks public sector companies.
Last week Standard & Poor's signed an agreement to buy 9.6 percent equity holdings in CRISIL.
